terms.definition: The actual chance that something happens, such as 2 in 100 people. Changes in absolute risk show how many people are really affected.
How the chance of an outcome in one group compares with another, such as 50% lower. It can sound large even when few people are affected.
A study in which people are assigned by chance to receive a treatment or a comparison. Chance assignment makes the groups alike, so a difference in outcomes can be credited to the treatment.
A study that records what people already do without assigning treatments. It can show that two things go together, but not reliably that one causes the other.
A method that combines the results of several studies on the same question into one estimate.
A review that searches for all the studies on a question using a method set out in advance, then appraises and summarizes them.
An inactive treatment made to look like the real one. It lets researchers separate the effect of a treatment from the effect of expecting to be treated.
The group in a study that does not receive the treatment being tested. It is the baseline the treated group is compared with.
Keeping participants, researchers, or both from knowing who received which treatment, so that expectations do not shape the results.
When a third factor is linked to both the suspected cause and the outcome, creating an association that is not causal.
A tendency for two things to rise or fall together. On its own it does not show that one causes the other.
The number of participants or observations in a study. Larger samples give more precise estimates.
A measure of how large a difference or relationship is, as opposed to whether one was detected.
A range of values consistent with the data. A wide interval means the estimate is imprecise.
The probability of seeing a result at least this extreme if there were truly no effect. It is not the probability that the finding is wrong.
A result unlikely to arise by chance alone under a set threshold, often a p-value below 0.05. It says nothing about whether the effect is large enough to matter.
Evaluation of a study by other researchers in the field before a journal publishes it. It screens for problems but does not guarantee the findings are correct.
A study shared publicly before peer review. Its findings may change before, or never reach, publication in a journal.
